reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the shared ledger myself. I'll start by listing the orders to see what's there.
Alpha Co says refunds for orders 292 and 294 are applied, but I should confirm that on the shared ledger before paying anyone. I'll list the refunds.
The shared ledger matches Alpha Co's report: refunds for orders 292 and 294 are applied with the stated amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 40355 matches its orders (4834 + 35521) with no refunds, so the figure is consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 40935 matches its orders (36109 + 15074) minus the applied refund on order 294 (10248). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
Cobalt's net of 34770 matches its orders (9909 + 27790) minus the refund on order 292 (2929). All three balances reconcile with the ledger, so I'll record payouts now, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 40355 was recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 40935 reconciles with its orders minus the refund on order 294, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 34770 reconciles with its orders minus the refund on order 292, and birch's payout went through, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each one matches the orders minus the applied refunds: acme 40355, birch 40935, cobalt 34770. The batch is complete.
